## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Muttātherīgāthā* (Thig 1.2) is the second poem of the *Therīgāthā* in the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. In a study of monastic rules and traditions concerning nuns, Bhikkhu Sujato observes that editorial rubrics framing the verse record that it was frequently taught by the Buddha to Muttā while she was a probationer or trainee nun (*sikkhamānā*) [Sujato 2009]. Sujato points out, however, that the poetic verse itself contains no indications of her probationary status or age, and the commentary provides no additional information, indicating that the rubric is an editorial note supplied by later redactors [Sujato 2009].

Curated records on SuttaCentral identify no parallels for this verse in other Buddhist collections [SuttaCentral]. In agreement with this, automated cross-language and internal text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identified no significant Pali-internal reuse and no cross-language matches in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral documents thirteen modern translations into ten languages, including English versions by Ayya Soma and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
